explanation: Smart pointers are template classes in C++ that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They are used to implement RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom, which ties resource lifetime to object lifetime, simplifying memory management and exception safety in modern C++ programming.

example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of 'std::unique_ptr' for exclusive ownership, which automatically deletes the managed object when it goes out of scope, exemplifying RAII. This illustrates how smart pointers facilitate safe and automatic memory management in modern C++.
